title: Is 4 Bits Enough for EEG Sleep Staging? A Subject-Level Benchmark of MXFP4, NVFP4 and FP8
abstract: arXiv:2611.31436v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Staging sleep on a wearable device keeps the raw electroencephalogram (EEG) private and saves the energy needed to transmit it. It also requires small, energy-efficient neural networks. We benchmark 13 post-training quantization (PTQ) configurations, from FP16 to the block-scaled 4-bit formats MXFP4 and NVFP4, for five-stage sleep staging from single-channel Fpz-Cz EEG. We use Sleep-EDF-78 (78 subjects), subject-wise cross-validation, three training seeds, value-exact emulation, and per-subject paired statistics. All 8- and 16-bit formats stay within 0.45 percentage points (pp) of FP32 Macro-F1. With 4-bit weights and activations, an epoch-wise CNN loses 1.98 to 3.04 pp, and a temporal-context network loses at most 1.19 pp. A same-encoder ablation shows that temporal context explains little of this gap. At equal block size, NVFP4 outperforms MXFP4. The first layer, which quantizes the raw EEG, is the most sensitive layer in both networks

translated_title: 4比特足以用于脑电睡眠分期吗？MXFP4、NVFP4和FP8的受试者级别基准测试
translated_abstract: 在可穿戴设备上进行睡眠分期可以保护原始脑电图（EEG）数据的隐私，并节省传输所需的能量，但这同时也需要小型、节能的神经网络。我们对13种训练后量化（PTQ）配置进行了基准测试，范围涵盖FP16到块缩放的4位格式MXFP4和NVFP4，任务是基于单通道Fpz-Cz脑电信号进行五阶段睡眠分期。我们使用了Sleep-EDF-78数据集（78名受试者）、受试者级别的交叉验证、三个训练随机种子、数值精确仿真以及针对每位受试者的配对统计。结果显示，所有8位和16位格式与FP32的Macro-F1差距均保持在0.45个百分点以内。使用4位权重和激活值时，逐epoch的CNN损失1.98至3.04个百分点，而时间上下文网络最多损失1.19个百分点。相同编码器的消融实验表明，时间上下文对这一性能差距的解释作用很小。在相同块大小下，NVFP4优于MXFP4。量化原始脑电信号的第一层是两种网络中最敏感的层。
tldr: 该论文首次在受试者级别系统评估了FP16至4位块缩放格式（MXFP4、NVFP4）及FP8在脑电睡眠分期中的量化性能，发现8/16位量化几乎无损，4位量化下时间上下文网络最多仅损失1.19个百分点，且NVFP4优于MXFP4，其中量化原始脑电信号的第一层最为敏感。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first subject-level benchmark of post-training quantization from FP16 down to 4-bit block-scaled formats (MXFP4, NVFP4) and FP8 for EEG sleep staging, showing that 8/16-bit formats are nearly lossless, a temporal-context network loses at most 1.19 pp in Macro-F1 at 4-bit precision, NVFP4 outperforms MXFP4 at equal block size, and the first layer quantizing raw EEG is the most sensitive.
